title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, NFTs, Web3 and crypto regulation.

title: Decentralized email platform Dmail to cease services on May 15
summary: Dmail Network will shut down on May 15 after citing high infrastructure costs, failed fundraising and weak token utility.

title: Centralizing crypto: Why Malta’s clash with ESMA is about more than one small state
summary: A plan to move supervision of major crypto asset service providers to the France-based ESMA is testing MiCA’s balance between EU-level control and national-level decision-making.

title: Aave avoided bad debt by shifting risk to borrowers: Bank of Canada study
summary: A Bank of Canada staff paper found Aave V3 avoided bad debt in 2024, but said the model pushed losses onto borrowers during liquidations.

title: Bitcoin 'done' with 85% crashes, says Cathie Wood amid new $34K target
summary: ARK Invest CEO Cathie Wood said that Bitcoin as a "proven" asset would no longer experience drawdowns of 85% or more from all-time highs.

title: Drift sends onchain message to wallets tied to $280M exploit
summary: Drift Protocol initiated onchain contact with wallets tied to the $280 million exploit as an unknown sender also attempts to pressure the attacker.

title: South Korean brokerage Korea Investment & Securities eyes Coinone stake: Report
summary: The reported acquisition talks come as South Korea is considering a 20% cap on major crypto exchange shareholders, which would force major platforms to restructure ownership.

title: Crypto hackers steal $169M from 34 DeFi protocols in Q1: DefiLlama
summary: January saw the largest attack against a DeFi protocol of the quarter, the $40 million private key compromise of portfolio management platform Step Finance.

title: Bitcoin supply in profit heads to ‘true bear market’ levels
summary: CryptoQuant data shows there are 8.2 million Bitcoin currently at a loss, which is still under the amount of Bitcoin at a loss during the 2022 bear market.

title: Tokenization makes finance more efficient but introduces risks: IMF
summary: The IMF said tokenization could improve cross-border payments and financial inclusion in emerging economies but cited concerns over volatility and the “erosion of monetary sovereignty.”
